prompt: Hypothetical. Swing low Rs 200, swing high Rs 260. What is the 38.2 percent retracement level?
Hypothetical. Swing low Rs 300, swing high Rs 340. What is the 50 percent retracement level?
solution: Range = 340 - 300 = 40. Ratio x range = 0.50 x 40 = 20. Level = 340 - 20 = Rs 320. The 50 percent level is a convention, so the level is half the range.

prompt: Hypothetical. Swing low Rs 200, swing high Rs 240. What is the 23.6 percent retracement level?
Hypothetical. Swing low Rs 200, swing high Rs 260. Why would a different swing low give different levels?

options.text: Because the range is measured from the swing high to the swing low, so a different low gives a different range
Because the ratios change with the calendar date
Because Fibonacci levels are fixed prices that are the same on every chart

explanations.b: The ratios are fixed numbers. The date does not change them. The range does change when the swing low changes.
explanations.c: The levels are not fixed prices. They come from the swing points you choose, so they change when those points change.
explanations.d: Volume is not part of the formula. The levels come only from the swing high, the swing low and the ratio.

prompt: Hypothetical. A reader draws levels after a fall. The price pauses at the 61.8 percent level. The reader writes, 'This level guarantees a bounce, so I will buy here.' Which response fits the book's rules?

options.text: Agree. A Fibonacci level is a reliable sign that the price will bounce
Treat the level as a zone to watch. Test any rule before using it, and set the stop and size before any order
Ignore all levels, because no level can ever be useful
Use the 61.8 percent price as an exact stop, because the ratio is a known number

explanations.a: No level guarantees a bounce. The evidence that these levels predict price is contested, and a pause at a level does not prove a turn.
explanations.c: Levels can describe where price has reacted before. The mistake is treating them as certain, not treating them as useless.
explanations.d: The ratio is a convention applied to a chosen range. The exact stop depends on the swing points, and a stop still needs a tested rule and a stated loss.

prompt: Read this statement. Which part is wrong? 'The 50 percent level is a true Fibonacci ratio. It is half of the swing range, so the level is useful.'

options.text: The 50 percent level is a true Fibonacci ratio
It is half of the swing range
There is no mistake in the statement

explanations.b: This part is correct. Half of the range is 50 percent of the range. The mistake is in the first part of the statement.
explanations.c: There is a mistake. The 50 percent level is included as a convention. It is not a Fibonacci ratio in the strict sense.
